description: Numbers — plain text, decimals, dates, percentages, units, and numbers inside math.

num_hanzi.description: Number directly followed by hanzi → hyphen ⠤ (the number cell and the hanzi's first cell collide in shape; without separation it reads as a continuation of the number)

cases.note: 页's leading cell ⠑=5: without separation 10页 reads as 105
个's leading cell ⠛=7: without separation 3个 reads as 37

date.description: Dates (year/month/day recognized by the normalizer as a Date node)

cases.note: year only: digits + 年(nian2); 年 is the sole exception to the hyphen/connector, written directly attached
date components are space-separated (年 / 5月); within a component the number attaches to its marker — 年 directly (no separator), 月 via the hyphen/connector ⠤
year/month/day components are space-separated (2026年 5月 17日); within each, the number attaches to its marker — 年 directly, 月/日 via the hyphen/connector ⠤ (日's ⠚=0, so 17日 needs the ⠤)
the ordinal prefix 第 binds to a digit-led date exactly as to a bare number (第3): no space — it used to take the composite's word-boundary space and split 第 from its own year

a date followed by a number (…31日23时) takes the composite's word-boundary space — 日's tone cell must not run straight into 23's number sign — matching the date-internal component spacing; 23时 keeps the number→hanzi connector ⠤

fullwidth.description: Full-width digits with full-width separators fold to their half-width spellings — cell-for-cell identical, no warnings (the ideographic 。 is sentence punctuation and never a decimal)

cases.note: pure full-width digit run: the prose backend folds each digit at render time
full-width decimal point ． folds into the digit run as its ASCII separator — same cells as 3.5 (it used to die as UNKNOWN_PUNCT plus a split number)
full-width comma folds the same way, aligned with half-width thousands behavior — same cells as 3,500 (it used to render the comma as prose punct ⠐ and split the number with no warning at all)
full-width decimal with unit: identical to 3.5米
the ideographic full stop 。 is the Chinese sentence end, never a decimal point: the number splits, unlike its full-width twin ．

percent.description: Percent sign — a Number beside a Punct, with the spacing in the punctuation table

cases.note: percent sign ⠨ after digits, then %'s own space_after. The trailing blank is the raw cell stream; the layout renderer trims a line's trailing blanks, exactly as it does for the comma in '你，'
a percentage is a whole word, and the blank that says so is %'s space_after — it used to need a composite IR node because the table could not express it
no blank before the comma: the mark is written against the word it follows, so its table entry vetoes the separator %'s space_after asked for
one blank, not two: %'s space_after and the author's own space both land here and the adjacent-blank merge keeps the typed one
3 kg: digits + one latin_lower sign for the unit run (docx 计量单位 例1: 47cm → ⠼⠙⠛⠰⠉⠍)

a number+unit abutting Chinese takes a word boundary — and the blank comes from the latin↔hanzi rule, not from any composite node: the same text with a non-unit run (3.5foo重) renders with the identical structure, which is why there is no unit table
